paras: The threatened lynching of Frank Polonious occurred about late September 1888 near Mahanoy City, when passengers on a Lehigh Valley passenger train nearly lynched an eighteen-year-old Hungarian caught trying to wreck it with a stone on the track. He was not harmed, and in November he pleaded guilty and was sentenced to three and a half years in prison and a $500 fine.

According to the account he gave in court, Polonious had been brought to "this country" under contract six months before the attempt. He then lost his work and was, in the dispatch's words, "friendless and starving."

Knowing a train was due, he said, he sat on the track meaning to let it kill him, until the idea of putting a stone "in the frog in the cut" came to him as "revenge for his helplessness." He was caught in the attempt, though the report does not say by whom. When the passengers learned of their narrow escape, he "narrowly escaped lynching at the time" at their hands; the dispatch gives no further detail of what they did or how he was saved.

A Pottsville dispatch of November 26 reported that Polonious had pleaded guilty and been sentenced to three and a half years' imprisonment and a $500 fine. No report of any action against the passengers appears in the coverage.

The only account found is the sentencing dispatch as reprinted by the Daily Kennebec Journal of Augusta, Maine, on November 27, 1888, under "Crimes and Accidents." Headlined "A Train Wrecker Sentenced" with the subhead "Friendless and Despondent He Thought to Take Revenge on the World," it centered on his crime and motive and mentioned the near-lynching only in its last sentence, without comment. No report of the attempted wreck from September was found.

Polonious was not killed; the passengers, who had no lawful authority, are said only to have nearly lynched him in anger at the attempted wreck, and their number is not given (A2).
One reprint of a Pottsville dispatch, published two months after the event, is the only account, and it gives the near-lynching in a single sentence (A2).

info: About two months before a Pottsville dispatch dated November 26, 1888, i.e. about late September 1888
On the Lehigh Valley line near Mahanoy City ('Mahonoy City'), at a frog in a cut
Frank Polonious, eighteen, described as Hungarian
Attempting to wreck a passenger train by placing a large stone on the track; he was caught in the act, according to the dispatch
Sentenced to three and a half years' imprisonment and fined $500
